finish_summary: Implemented popcount32 using an explicit balanced binary adder tree (pairwise combining bits into progressively wider partial sums: 2-bit → 3-bit → 4-bit → 5-bit → 6-bit) instead of the original flat chain of 31 additions, while preserving identical synchronous reset, valid_o pipeline, and hold-on-invalid behavior for y_o. Verified via place_and_route: area 264.67 µm² (unchanged from baseline), WNS 7.01662 ns (marginally better than baseline's 7.01636 ns), yielding a score of 69.90153 vs. the baseline's 69.89893. Analysis showed that both the naive chain and the balanced-tree codings synthesize to the same minimal-area netlist under Yosys/ABC's optimization, indicating this is near the practical floor for area given the fixed 32-bit popcount function and Nangate45 cell library; further logic restructurings (e.g., SWAR bit-trick formulas, explicit half/full-adder compressor networks, behavioral for-loop descriptions) are functionally equivalent and would very likely converge to the same or a very similar synthesized result, so no further place_and_route budget was spent on them. Finalizing with the balanced-tree version as the best verified result.
